quizzes.title: Getting Started Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction to Python, Variables, Types & Input, Operators & Conditions.

questions.prompt: How does Python group the lines inside an if statement?
questions.explanation: Python uses indentation (usually 4 spaces) instead of braces. The wrong indentation is a syntax error.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: 5 is an int, 5.0 is a float and "5" in quotes is a str. print shows the full class names.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: // is floor division (3), % is the remainder (1) and ** is the power (8).

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: An f-string evaluates whatever is inside { }: upper() gives SARA and len gives 4.

questions.prompt: What type does input() always return?
options: It depends on what the user types
questions.explanation: input() always gives text. Convert it with int() or float() when you need a number.

questions.prompt: Complete the condition so that a person who is exactly 18 counts as an adult.
questions.explanation: >= means "greater than or equal to", so 18 passes. A plain > would not.

quizzes.title: Data & Control Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Loops, Lists & Tuples, Dictionaries & Sets, Functions.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: range(start, stop, step) stops before stop. 2, 4, 6 are printed and 8 is not reached.
questions.code:
for i in range(2, 8, 2):
    print(i, end=" ")

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: A slice [1:3] takes indexes 1 and 2 (the end is excluded). Index -1 is the last item.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: get() returns the default (0) for a missing key instead of an error. The dict has 2 keys by then.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: f(5) uses the default y=10, so 15. f(5, y=1) uses y=1, so 6.

questions.prompt: Which of these cannot be changed after it is created?
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable. Lists, dictionaries and sets can be changed.

questions.prompt: Complete the code so it prints the squares of 1, 2 and 3.
questions.code:
squares = [n * n for n in ____(1, 4)]
print(squares)
questions.explanation: range(1, 4) gives 1, 2, 3. The comprehension squares each number.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: __init__ stored "Rex" in self.name, and speak() uses it.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: int("abc") raises ValueError, so the except block runs. finally always runs afterwards.

questions.prompt: What does "with open(...) as f:" do for you?
options: Opens the file in a new window
Closes the file automatically, even if an error happens
Creates a copy of the file
questions.explanation: The with statement guarantees the file is closed when the block ends.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: B overrides hi() but calls the parent's version with super(), so "B" + "A".

questions.prompt: Which file mode erases the old content before writing?
questions.explanation: "w" opens for writing and truncates the file. "a" appends and "r" only reads.

questions.prompt: Complete the keyword that signals an error.
questions.explanation: raise throws an exception that the except block can catch.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: The comprehension keeps only the even numbers from 1 to 6 (2, 4, 6) and squares them, giving [4, 16, 36].
questions.code: print([n * n for n in range(1, 7) if n % 2 == 0])

questions.prompt: What does the yield keyword do inside a function?
options: Raises an error to the caller
Hands back a value and pauses the function so it can resume later
questions.explanation: yield turns the function into a generator. Each next() call runs it until the next yield, and it continues from there on the following call.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: Each next() call resumes the generator until the next yield. The first call gives 3 and the second gives 2.

questions.prompt: What does the @shout line above def add(a, b) do?
options: It is the same as writing add = shout(add)
It turns add into a class
questions.explanation: A decorator is shorthand for passing the function to another function and using the result in its place: add = shout(add).

questions.prompt: Which statement makes sure cleanup code, such as closing a file, runs even if an error happens inside the block?
questions.explanation: with uses a context manager. Its __exit__ method always runs when the block ends, even after an exception.

questions.prompt: Complete the line that turns the class into a dataclass.
questions.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass

____
class Student:
    name: str
    marks: int = 0

print(Student("Ali", 80))
questions.explanation: The @dataclass decorator generates __init__, __repr__ and __eq__ from the annotated fields, so print shows Student(name='Ali', marks=80).
